jobs.title: Deputy Director of Institutional Giving
jobs.description:
Employment Type

Full-Time/Exempt

Wage

$115,000 - $125,000 base pay

Department

Philanthropy

Reports To

Director of Institutional Giving

Position Location

California – Oakland, Los Angeles, Sacramento, Riverside, Fresno

Work Schedule

Four Day Work Week: Two (2) days in office, two (2) days remote. However, there may be certain circumstances, like pressing deadlines or peak business periods, where it becomes necessary for the organization to temporarily switch to a five-day work week.

WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW

California will define the next decade of climate action, and the resources behind that work have to keep pace. EnviroVoters is scaling its institutional funding program, and we need a senior fundraiser who can lead people, own strategy, and represent the organization with our most important foundation partners. This role sits at the center of a growing team, shaping how we cultivate funders, build the pipeline, and turn ambitious climate and justice campaigns into sustained investment.

This is a leadership role. The Deputy Director of Institutional Giving manages grant staff, drives portfolio strategy across both EnviroVoters (501c4) and the EnviroVoters Education Fund (501c3), and serves as a senior relationship holder with institutional funders. If you have led teams, closed six-figure grants, and want your work to fuel real political power, we want to hear from you.

What Makes This Role Distinctive

Four-day work week for most of the year with five-day weeks during peak periods
Management of a growing institutional giving team, with authority to shape systems, strategy, and portfolio assignments
Ownership of a portfolio of the organization's most significant institutional funders, with direct responsibility for cultivation, solicitation, and negotiation
A leadership seat in departmental planning, revenue forecasting, and annual budgeting
Dual-entity fundraising across c3 and c4 structures, work that few institutional giving roles offer
Comprehensive benefits package, including health, vision and dental coverage, 401(k) with employer match,12 days PTO, 12 holidays, a year-end office closure between Christmas and New Year, and additional benefits that support employee well-being and work-life balance

Position Summary

As a senior member of the Philanthropy Team, the Deputy Director of Institutional Giving leads the day-to-day operation and growth of the institutional giving program for EnviroVoters and the Ed Fund. This role manages grant staff and consultants, owns a portfolio of high-priority institutional funders, drives annual grant strategy and revenue planning in partnership with the Director of Institutional Giving, and ensures the full grant lifecycle runs with excellence across both entities.

KEY PRIORITIES

Lead and develop the institutional giving team

Manage grant staff and consultants supporting the institutional giving portfolio, including hiring, coaching, and performance development
Set portfolio assignments, workflows, and quality standards across proposals, reports, and stewardship activities
Evaluate and strengthen systems and processes for grants management, ensuring compliance and alignment with organizational values

Own strategic funder relationships

Manage a portfolio of the organization's largest and most complex institutional funders, leading cultivation, solicitation, negotiation, and stewardship
Represent EnviroVoters and the Ed Fund with funders and program officers, including independently leading meetings, pitches, and site visits

Drive portfolio strategy and revenue growth

Support in the execution of an annual institutional giving strategy aligned with organizational priorities and revenue goals
Expand the funder pipeline by identifying, researching, and cultivating new institutional prospects for both entities
Support the Director of Institutional Giving in annual budgeting, revenue forecasting, and monthly revenue reporting

Ensure grant management excellence across both entities

Oversee production of multi-year and one-year proposals and reports, ensuring quality, accuracy, and timely delivery
Provide internal guidance on permissible grant usage across c3 and c4 entities, including compliance with lobbying and electoral activity restrictions
Project manage complex, cross-departmental proposal development and ensure funding agreements are finalized, signed, and paid on schedule
Work proactively with program, policy, and finance staff to meet all programmatic and fiscal reporting requirements

What We Need From You

Seven or more years of institutional fundraising experience in a nonprofit environment, including demonstrated success securing and renewing five- and six-figure grants
Two or more years of staff management experience, with a track record of coaching and developing fundraising or grants professionals
Expertise in cultivating and stewarding external funder relationships, including leading solicitations and negotiations independently
Working knowledge of 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) fundraising distinctions, or demonstrated ability to learn and apply them quickly
Deep understanding of the full grant lifecycle and grant writing craft, with the ability to edit and elevate the work of others
Ability to manage multiple proposals, deadlines, staff, and stakeholders simultaneously under pressure
Skilled in persuasive written and oral communication, with the ability to synthesize complex policy work into compelling cases for support
Exceptional attention to detail, discretion, and ability to maintain confidentiality
Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Raiser's Edge/RENXT or similar CRM preferred
Passionate about environmental protection, racial justice, and meaningful social change

Additional Strengths We Welcome

Experience fundraising for advocacy, electoral, or 501(c)(4) organizations
Familiarity with Community Centric Fundraising principles
Experience with project management tools such as Asana
Background in environmental policy, political science, communications, nonprofit management, public administration, or a related field

What Else You Should Know

California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund are committed to workplace diversity and inclusion. We are equal opportunity employers and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

EnviroVoters and EnviroVoters Ed Fund has a deep commitment to equity and fostering a culture of inclusion. We invite and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including those from groups traditionally underrepresented in employment, who may contribute to further diversifying our organization.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely do so because of an advertisement. They enroll because someone they trust looked them in the eye over dinner and said, "This transformed my child." You would be responsible for building and sustaining that word-of-mouth engine across an entire region: orchestrating the dinners, cultivating parent ambassadors, connecting with the mayor's office, and arranging for a CEO to open doors for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four different settings. You create and execute the region's event calendar—from open houses with 150 attendees to intimate, curated dinners for eight—multiple times each month. You identify and prepare current parents who are eager to share their experience with prospective families, then facilitate those one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting those relationships into event venues, backing for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: brokering introductions, coordinating expert-led masterclasses, arranging internships, integrating alumni, and recording each interaction family by family.

There is no complete manual. You build the system as you execute it, and the frameworks you develop become models for colleagues doing the same work in other markets. As your region expands, the performance bar rises rather than falls: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth driven by authentic advocacy—a metric tracked across years, not quarters.

No degree is required, and no specific institutional background is expected. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated ability to convene people and convert relationships into outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The position requires evening and weekend availability in settings with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and business founders, along with regular local travel. You will become the most networked individual in your city, and you will deploy that capital for the benefit of students. If that exchange sounds like purpose rather than sacrifice, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the region's event calendar: open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats—multiple per month, all within budget
Identifying and booking venues, hosts, and vendors, then personally facilitating each event
Identifying current parents to serve as ambassadors, training them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with municipal officials and corporate leaders, and translating those into event spaces, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and professional internships, and onboarding graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-touch attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, verifiable figure

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no media budgets, no targets based on impressions or lead volume
Controlling the brand narrative or enterprise-wide campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions logistics, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Managing the daily operations of a campus or overseeing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance figures and headcount as if a full room were the objective
Delaying action until a complete playbook, template, or support team is in place

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Establish people-driven referrals as the predominant source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years developing communities or relationship-based programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a similar network-driven business, where growth was driven by people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client portfolio, with quantifiable results
Personally planned and executed 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to open events with 100+ attendees, with responsibility for budget management
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or corporate executives that delivered specific, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM practitioner; consistently logging relationships, attributions, and activity is already standard practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community initiatives, or partnerships for a network-based organization: a school network, membership club, franchise system, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality roles, consistently selected to represent and host on behalf of the institution
Pre-existing relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deeply familiar with how families evaluate and decide on high-stakes education choices

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

Posted Job Title

Executive Director of Engagement Strategy and Systems

Job Profile Title

Information Technology Director

Job Description Summary

The Executive Director of Engagement Strategy and Systems serves as Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) senior leader responsible for the digital engagement strategy, drawing on constituent research, behavioral insights, and collaboration across advancement functions to create coordinated experiences that deepen alumni relationships and donor participation. As the senior functional and strategic owner of Penn’s engagement technology ecosystem, this role serves as the critical bridge connecting DAR’s communications and engagement strategy to the technical expertise required to manage the systems involved in digital engagement. The position entails specialized understanding and skills in effective constituent engagement supported by strategic data and technology decisions. This role’s success depends on knowing how platforms should be used to advance alumni and donor relationships, supporting users and adoption, evaluating effectiveness, and continuously improving the constituent experience. In doing so, the role ensures that DAR’s engagement work, including the systems that support these, are well governed, and strategically applied to achieve communications, engagement, and fundraising goals.

The Executive Director leads digital transformation and innovation across DAR’s engagement systems and serves as a strategic liaison to University technology partners. Under the guidance of the Senior Executive Director of Marketing and Communications, , the role provides leadership across governance, operating standards, data stewardship, architecture, integrations, and vendor strategy, while establishing department-wide frameworks that support secure, scalable, and user-centered experiences across schools and centers. The position exercises significant influence over decisions that advance engagement outcomes, donor pipeline development, and the Penn alumni experience worldwide.

Embedded within DAR Communications and Marketing, the Executive Director serves as a strategic advisor to University and DAR leadership, partnering closely with colleagues across central DAR and the schools and centers to advance institutional engagement priorities. The position leads a specialized team responsible for improving communications and marketing strategy through platform administration, optimization, training, adoption, and continuous improvement.

Job Description

Job Responsibilities

Digital Engagement Strategy

Lead the development of an enterprise digital engagement strategy that aligns communications, alumni relations, annual giving, events, volunteer engagement, and development priorities across DAR.
Partner with DAR Marketing and Communications, Alumni Relations, Annual Giving, development teams, analytics, and schools and centers to identify constituent needs, establish shared engagement priorities, and translate those priorities into coordinated digital experiences.
Determine alumni engagement strategies and provide strategic counsel to DAR senior leadership and ISC and lead efforts on resource prioritization, operational sustainability, and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies—including AI and automation—to strengthen constituent engagement and organizational effectiveness.
Develop and execute a multi-year digital engagement systems roadmap that supports DAR’s priorities and advances Penn’s mission.
Use audience research and engagement data to identify unmet needs, participation barriers, communication preferences, and opportunities to strengthen alumni relationships and giving.
Lead strategies for audience segmentation, personalization, communication preferences, and coordinated multichannel engagement across email, web, events, communities, mentoring, volunteer programs, and fundraising outreach.

Digital Engagement User Optimization and Support

Lead governance committees responsible for establishing and enforcing standards, ensuring execution of communications and engagement tactics are compliant and effective.
Support systems users by establishing standards and best practices for each tool to increase engagement; reviewing data analytics of engagement performance and fundraising outcomes; offering training and ongoing support, and continuous audit of systems use for measurable engagement outcomes.
Provide strategic and operational oversight for the selection, implementation, integration, and lifecycle management of communications and engagement platforms to support DAR’s engagement goals, including:
Constituent engagement through marketing automation and CRM systems (including Salesforce Marketing Cloud)
Event registration and program management
Mentoring and volunteer management
Alumni communities and websites (MyPenn, Club/SIG Communities)
Ensure systems are user-friendly, scalable, accessible, and continuously optimized.
Serve as the primary liaison to ISC Security and Compliance teams to ensure all engagement systems and practices align with University policies, privacy standards, and current cybersecurity requirements.
Ensure institutional compliance with global and federal data privacy regulations—including GDPR, CAN-SPAM, CCPA, and other emerging standards—through oversight of consent management, data protection practices, email compliance, and privacy-related workflows.

Platform Administration, Security, and Optimization

Oversee implementation and administration of engagement platforms, guiding system architecture, data integrations, accessibility, and continuous improvement.

Innovation & Continuous Improvement

Stay current on trends in strategic communications, digital engagement for alumni relations and fundraising, engagement technologies, user experience, and data governance.
Identify opportunities for automation, AI-driven engagement, enhanced analytics, and improved alumni and donor experience.
Recommend and implement innovative tools that strengthen alumni and donor engagement and staff effectiveness.

Team Leadership

Lead and develop a team to drive strategic digital engagement, support related platform governance and administration; user training, support, and compliance; and engagement data analytics.
Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Collaboration & Vendor Management

Develop and maintain strong cross-functional relationships across DAR to drive consistent alumni and donor engagement strategies.
Lead strategic planning and stewardship of engagement technology investments in service to DAR’s engagement and fundraising goals.
Partner closely with ISC and teams across DAR to develop system strategy and ensure alignment, compliance, and interoperability.
Lead vendor relationships, contract negotiations, RFP processes, and service-level monitoring of DAR’s engagement tools.
Please provide a resume and cover letter in order to be considered for this role. Please upload all documents in the “Resume/CV” section of the application prior to submitting.**

Qualifications

Bachelor of Science and 5 to 7 years of experience or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of 7–10 years of progressively responsible experience in advancement communications, digital engagement strategy, constituent experience, and marketing technology deployment preferred.
Experience working in higher education, nonprofit advancement, alumni relations, fundraising, or mission-driven organizations strongly preferred.
Experience using Salesforce technologies for constituent engagement, including Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP), and related engagement or CRM platforms.
Understanding of platform governance, cybersecurity best practices, identity and access management, audit processes, and institutional risk mitigation.
Knowledge of data privacy regulations and digital compliance standards, including GDPR, CAN-SPAM, CCPA, accessibility standards, and emerging digital governance requirements involved in marketing and constituent engagement.
Experience working with technology vendors, contract negotiations, procurement processes, and strategic technology partnerships.
Proven leadership and staff management experience, including the ability to mentor teams, manage performance, and foster collaboration and innovation.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to balance strategic planning and operational execution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical concepts and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and non-technical audiences.
Familiarity with emerging technologies related to AI-enabled engagement, automation, analytics, and digital constituent experience strategies preferred. erience is required.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely do so because of an advertisement. They enroll because someone they trust looked them in the eye over dinner and said, "This transformed my child." You would be responsible for building and sustaining that word-of-mouth engine across an entire region: orchestrating the dinners, cultivating parent ambassadors, connecting with the mayor's office, and arranging for a CEO to open doors for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four different settings. You create and execute the region's event calendar—from open houses with 150 attendees to intimate, curated dinners for eight—multiple times each month. You identify and prepare current parents who are eager to share their experience with prospective families, then facilitate those one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting those relationships into event venues, backing for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: brokering introductions, coordinating expert-led masterclasses, arranging internships, integrating alumni, and recording each interaction family by family.

There is no complete manual. You build the system as you execute it, and the frameworks you develop become models for colleagues doing the same work in other markets. As your region expands, the performance bar rises rather than falls: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth driven by authentic advocacy—a metric tracked across years, not quarters.

No degree is required, and no specific institutional background is expected. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated ability to convene people and convert relationships into outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The position requires evening and weekend availability in settings with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and business founders, along with regular local travel. You will become the most networked individual in your city, and you will deploy that capital for the benefit of students. If that exchange sounds like purpose rather than sacrifice, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the region's event calendar: open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats—multiple per month, all within budget
Identifying and booking venues, hosts, and vendors, then personally facilitating each event
Identifying current parents to serve as ambassadors, training them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with municipal officials and corporate leaders, and translating those into event spaces, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and professional internships, and onboarding graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-touch attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, verifiable figure

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no media budgets, no targets based on impressions or lead volume
Controlling the brand narrative or enterprise-wide campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions logistics, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Managing the daily operations of a campus or overseeing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance figures and headcount as if a full room were the objective
Delaying action until a complete playbook, template, or support team is in place

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Establish people-driven referrals as the predominant source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years developing communities or relationship-based programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a similar network-driven business, where growth was driven by people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client portfolio, with quantifiable results
Personally planned and executed 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to open events with 100+ attendees, with responsibility for budget management
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or corporate executives that delivered specific, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM practitioner; consistently logging relationships, attributions, and activity is already standard practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community initiatives, or partnerships for a network-based organization: a school network, membership club, franchise system, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality roles, consistently selected to represent and host on behalf of the institution
Pre-existing relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deeply familiar with how families evaluate and decide on high-stakes education choices

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

jobs.title: Program Director, GT School (Remote) - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
You've already taken something from concept to scale. You're now looking for your next meaningful challenge—one with real stakes and moral purpose. If you're convinced the U.S. education system is failing gifted students in unacceptable ways, and you're prepared to act on that conviction, this role is worth your attention.

gt.school is redesigning schooling for high-potential learners. Our 2 Hour Learning approach condenses the academic curriculum into concentrated, mastery-driven sessions—creating space for students to engage with meaningful challenges. Our next step is to establish a physical model campus that provides what's been missing: leadership development, competitive peer environments, a performance-oriented culture, and genuine community.

In this role, you will oversee the design, validation, and public launch of the model campus—with the aim of establishing it as the blueprint for a national expansion. You'll also continue developing our virtual GT Anywhere program alongside the existing team. This involves piloting real-world programming, cultivating parent demand, embedding lasting culture, and creating scalable operational frameworks.

We're looking for someone with founder-level drive and standing. Someone who knows that vision without execution is meaningless. Someone who can transform a clear perspective into a school that parents advocate for—and students are eager to join.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and piloting scalable programs beyond the academic scope—centered on leadership development, independence, and competitive engagement
Establishing and validating a physical model campus, including operational frameworks, staffing structures, and facility design
Crafting parent-facing communications, market positioning, and expansion frameworks to support growth
Establishing, codifying, and scaling quality benchmarks and cultural practices for all future locations
Serving as the public representative of the model—building visibility through media appearances, events, and strategic partnerships

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating a conventional school with traditional classrooms, teachers, and full-day instruction
Serving families seeking watered-down gifted programs with AP courses and limited rigor
Leading incremental improvements within existing educational structures—we're not reforming schools, we're building an alternative
Pursuing shallow engagement indicators—we prioritize substantive outcomes and rigorous learning over mere activity
Working entirely remotely—while you'll have flexibility, you'll spend approximately 1 week per month in Austin to stay grounded in the work

Program Director Key Responsibilities

Design, validate, and scale a high-performance model for gifted education—beginning with a single prototype campus and growing into a national network.

Basic Requirements

Built and scaled a high-impact venture from scratch (bonus if it involved physical operations or education). We are talking about at least 1M USD yearly revenue owned by you
Deep, personal understanding of gifted students—whether through family, professional experience, or lived reality
AI First mentality — Inclination to prioritize AI as the default solution for problem-solving, decision-making and work output generation at scale.
Proven ability to articulate a compelling vision and convert skeptics into believers
Based in the U.S., with ability to travel regularly to Austin (minimum 1 week/month)
Eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

About GT School

GT School is revolutionizing education with AI, expert coaching, and 50+ years of learning science. They blend cutting-edge tech with data-driven insights to unlock every student's full potential.

They're on a mission to disrupt the broken education system and unleash the true potential of gifted minds. Forget the one-size-fits-all approach that leaves brilliant students bored and disengaged.

This school has tossed the rulebook and created a modern learning environment powered by AI and guided by dedicated mentors. Their personalized approach accelerates learning - 2-6 times faster than traditional classrooms.

GT School students explore their passions, develop critical thinking skills, and learn to innovate.

Because that's where genius lies.

GT School is where gifted minds turn potential into power.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $200 USD/hour, which equates to $400,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely do so because of an advertisement. They enroll because someone they trust looked them in the eye over dinner and said, "This transformed my child." You would be responsible for building and sustaining that word-of-mouth engine across an entire region: orchestrating the dinners, cultivating parent ambassadors, connecting with the mayor's office, and arranging for a CEO to open doors for a 14-year-old's first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four different settings. You create and execute the region's event calendar—from open houses with 150 attendees to intimate, curated dinners for eight—multiple times each month. You identify and prepare current parents who are eager to share their experience with prospective families, then facilitate those one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting those relationships into event venues, backing for new campus launches, and tangible opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks promise: brokering introductions, coordinating expert-led masterclasses, arranging internships, integrating alumni, and recording each interaction family by family.

There is no complete manual. You build the system as you execute it, and the frameworks you develop become models for colleagues doing the same work in other markets. As your region expands, the performance bar rises rather than falls: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth driven by authentic advocacy—a metric tracked across years, not quarters.

No degree is required, and no specific institutional background is expected. An MBA, a background in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed career in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated ability to convene people and convert relationships into outcomes.

This role is based on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The position requires evening and weekend availability in settings with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and business founders, along with regular local travel. You will become the most networked individual in your city, and you will deploy that capital for the benefit of students. If that exchange sounds like purpose rather than sacrifice, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the region's event calendar: open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats—multiple per month, all within budget
Identifying and booking venues, hosts, and vendors, then personally facilitating each event
Identifying current parents to serve as ambassadors, training them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing relationships with municipal officials and corporate leaders, and translating those into event spaces, support for campus expansion, and opportunities for students
Connecting enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and professional internships, and onboarding graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and first-touch attribution in the CRM so that "doors opened per family" reflects an accurate, verifiable figure

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no media budgets, no targets based on impressions or lead volume
Controlling the brand narrative or enterprise-wide campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions logistics, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own those functions
Managing the daily operations of a campus or overseeing the physical facility
Treating raw attendance figures and headcount as if a full room were the objective
Delaying action until a complete playbook, template, or support team is in place

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Establish people-driven referrals as the predominant source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years developing communities or relationship-based programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or a similar network-driven business, where growth was driven by people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client portfolio, with quantifiable results
Personally planned and executed 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to open events with 100+ attendees, with responsibility for budget management
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or corporate executives that delivered specific, identifiable value
Disciplined CRM practitioner; consistently logging relationships, attributions, and activity is already standard practice
Currently resides in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community initiatives, or partnerships for a network-based organization: a school network, membership club, franchise system, or civic or faith-based institution
Developed and monetized a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality roles, consistently selected to represent and host on behalf of the institution
Pre-existing relationships with local government or business leaders in your city
Deeply familiar with how families evaluate and decide on high-stakes education choices

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

jobs.title: Director of Development - Penn Engineering
jobs.description:
University Overview

The University of Pennsylvania, the largest private employer in Philadelphia, is a world-renowned leader in education, research, and innovation. This historic, Ivy League school consistently ranks among the top 10 universities in the annual U.S. News & World Report survey. Penn has 12 highly-regarded schools that provide opportunities for undergraduate, graduate and continuing education, all influenced by Penn’s distinctive interdisciplinary approach to scholarship and learning. As an employer Penn has been ranked nationally on many occasions with the most recent award from Forbes who named Penn one of America’s Best Large Employers in 2023.

Penn offers a unique working environment within the city of Philadelphia. The University is situated on a beautiful urban campus, with easy access to a range of educational, cultural, and recreational activities. With its historical significance and landmarks, lively cultural offerings, and wide variety of atmospheres, Philadelphia is the perfect place to call home for work and play.

The University offers a competitive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare and tuition benefits for employees and their families, generous retirement benefits, a wide variety of professional development opportunities, supportive work and family benefits, a wealth of health and wellness programs and resources, and much more.

Posted Job Title

Director of Development - Penn Engineering

Job Profile Title

Director D, Development, Fundraising

Job Description Summary

Penn Engineering’s world-acclaimed faculty, state-of-the-art research laboratories and highly interdisciplinary curricula offer an experience that is unparalleled. Innovation and technology drive every program and transform the fundamentals of what future engineers are learning. http://www.seas.upenn.edu/

Penn Engineering is seeking an accomplished and collaborative development professional to serve as the Director of Development. This is an exciting opportunity for a senior advancement professional with strong management and front-line fundraising skills to partner with a highly successful development and alumni relations team, an engaged Dean and Board, and a committed and involved community consisting of alumni, parents, faculty and friends.

Job Description

Reporting to the Vice Dean for Development and Alumni Relations, the Director of Development provides strategic leadership for fundraising and engagement efforts. This role leads a team of major gift officers and is responsible for the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of prospects who can make gifts of $125K or more.

Job Responsibilities

Manage a portfolio of 100 major and leadership gift prospects and develop and execute cultivation, solicitation and stewardship strategies to secure support for the School’s strategic priorities.
Identify and develop a pipeline of high-level gift prospects for immediate and long-term cultivation with a goal of growing the pool of top prospects who can provide significant philanthropic support for the School.
Lead and manage a team of major gift officers, setting clear goals, evaluating performance, and supporting professional development to drive strong results across key fundraising metrics.
Articulate and communicate Penn Engineering’s strategic priorities, aspirations, and values to alumni, parents and friends through informal and formal communications, including written proposals.
Work with the Central DAR data alignment team to analyze data, create portfolio strategies and develop a data driven program to maximize the engagement of the Penn Engineering community.
Work closely with the Vice Dean to develop annual goals, plans, and budgets for a comprehensive, strategy-driven fundraising program and participate in the development and execution of a comprehensive plan to maximize the success of Penn Engineering’s fundraising efforts.
Partner with the Dean, Vice Dean for Development and Alumni Relations and other academic and administrative leaders across the School and University to maximize support for the School.
Please provide a resume and cover letter in order to be considered for this role. Please upload all documents in the “Resume/CV” section of the application prior to submitting.**

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and 7 to 10 years of fundraising experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Demonstrated success managing a portfolio of high-capacity prospects. Exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, with experience engaging senior leadership, faculty, and high-level external stakeholders. Proven experience supervising and developing professional staff, including goal-setting, performance management, and coaching. Advanced professional skills in complex problem-solving, decision-making, and navigating multifaceted donor situations. Must hold a valid driver's license. Position involves extensive travel and evening/weekend work.

Job Location - City, State

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Department / School

Development and Alumni Relations

Pay Range

$135,327.00 - $190,000.00 Annual Rate

Salary offers are made based on the candidate’s qualifications, experience, skills, and education as they directly relate to the requirements of the position, and in alignment with salary ranges based on external market data for the job’s level. Internal organization and peer data at Penn are also considered.

Equal Opportunity Statement

The University of Pennsylvania is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates are considered for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, creed, national origin (including shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics), citizenship status, age, disability, veteran status or any class protected under applicable federal, state or local law.

Special Requirements

Background checks may be required after a conditional job offer is made. Consideration of the background check will be tailored to the requirements of the job.

University Benefits

Health, Life, and Flexible Spending Accounts: Penn offers comprehensive medical, prescription, behavioral health, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits to protect you and your family’s health and welfare. You can also use flexible spending accounts to pay for eligible health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars.
Tuition: Take advantage of Penn's exceptional tuition benefits. You, your spouse, and your dependent children can get tuition assistance here at Penn. Your dependent children are also eligible for tuition assistance at other institutions.
Retirement: Penn offers generous retirement plans to help you save for your future. Penn’s Basic, Matching, and Supplemental retirement plans allow you to save for retirement on a pre-tax or Roth basis. Choose from a wide variety of investment options through TIAA and Vanguard.
Time Away from Work: Penn provides you with a substantial amount of time away from work during the course of the year. This allows you to relax, take vacations, attend to personal affairs, recover from illness or injury, spend time with family—whatever your personal needs may be.
Long-Term Care Insurance: In partnership with Genworth Financial, Penn offers faculty and staff (and your eligible family members) long-term care insurance to help you cover some of the costs of long-term care services received at home, in the community or in a nursing facility. If you apply when you’re newly hired, you won’t have to provide proof of good health or be subject to underwriting requirements. Eligible family members must always provide proof of good health and are subject to underwriting.
Wellness and Work-life Resources: Penn is committed to supporting our faculty and staff as they balance the competing demands of work and personal life. That’s why we offer a wide variety of programs and resources to help you care for your health, your family, and your work-life balance.
Professional and Personal Development: Penn provides an array of resources to help you advance yourself personally and professionally.
University Resources: As a member of the Penn community, you have access to a wide range of University resources as well as cultural and recreational activities. Take advantage of the University’s libraries and athletic facilities, or visit our arboretum and art galleries. There’s always something going on at Penn, whether it’s a new exhibit at the Penn Museum, the latest music or theater presentation at the Annenberg Center, or the Penn Relays at Franklin Field to name just a few examples. As a member of the Penn community, you’re right in the middle of the excitement—and you and your family can enjoy many of these activities for free.
Discounts and Special Services: From arts and entertainment to transportation and mortgages, you'll find great deals for University faculty and staff. Not only do Penn arts and cultural centers and museums offer free and discounted admission and memberships to faculty and staff. You can also enjoy substantial savings on other goods and services such as new cars from Ford and General Motors, cellular phone service plans, movie tickets, and admission to theme parks.
Flexible Work Hours: Flexible work options offer creative approaches for completing work while promoting balance between work and personal commitments. These approaches involve use of non-traditional work hours, locations, and/or job structures.
Penn Home Ownership Services: Penn offers a forgivable loan for eligible employees interested in buying a home or currently residing in West Philadelphia, which can be used for closing costs or home improvements.
Adoption Assistance: Penn will reimburse eligible employees on qualified expenses in connection with the legal adoption of an eligible child, such as travel or court fees, for up to two adoptions in your household.

To learn more, please visit: https://www.hr.upenn.edu/PennHR/benefits-pay

jobs.title: Director of Development, Alpha - $250,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families at Alpha Miami rely on trusted advisors across all areas of their lives. You will become the advisor they've been seeking in education.

You will be the first person they reach out to when uncertainty arises, when something doesn't feel quite right, or when they want to share a meaningful moment with someone who truly understands. You'll develop deep familiarity with each family—enough to sense their needs before they articulate them—and you'll possess the judgment and composure to respond with discretion, warmth, and apparent ease. Over time, your role will extend beyond the school itself. You'll become woven into the way these families experience this formative chapter of their lives.

Miami's private school landscape is tight-knit, highly networked, and intolerant of errors. A family's Alpha experience doesn't remain confined to campus—it ripples through the channels that influence perception: residential buildings, social clubs, yachts, charity events, and WhatsApp conversations that determine where other families submit applications. You'll navigate this terrain naturally, drawing on a career spent in environments where reputation is paramount and one mistake can eclipse years of success. You'll cultivate a community families want to protect—one where inclusion feels organic and referrals emerge because the experience justifies them.

Miami operates as a global hub by nature. You'll engage with families from Latin America, international corporate leaders, finance and technology professionals newly relocated to Miami, and households accustomed to mobility whose perspectives on education—and institutions broadly—are informed by experiences well beyond traditional American private schooling. Many navigate Miami, São Paulo, Bogotá, Madrid, and New York with the same ease others cross neighborhoods, and they'll evaluate Alpha against alternatives worldwide. The ideal candidate will be equally adept at managing cross-cultural family expectations—and the demand for seamless, sophisticated relationships—as they are at navigating Miami's established private school culture.

Alpha operates outside traditional school models. Students complete core academics in two hours daily through AI-powered applications, then dedicate remaining time to public speaking, critical thinking, and applied projects. No conventional lectures. No unnecessary assignments. Performance in the top 1% nationally.

Families who select Alpha have made a deliberate choice—and in a city where opinions are abundant and educational decisions signal status, they'll face constant scrutiny. You'll ensure they're never at a loss for how to respond. If sustaining that conviction through years of sophisticated, internationally informed skepticism feels burdensome, this position isn't suitable. If it represents the most compelling dialogue you could facilitate, continue reading.

Shape the school community's cultural foundation—the atmosphere, rituals, and implicit standards that foster belonging—ensuring Alpha becomes a place families take pride in, not merely a school they selected
Manage the complete parent relationship arc—from initial contact through enrollment, ongoing retention, and sustained advocacy—allowing faculty to concentrate on students while families maintain consistent access to someone they trust
Detect emerging concerns early and address them with the discretion and judgment that preserves confidence—including the more difficult determination of when a family isn't aligned with the school
Maintain physical presence where families gather: morning drop-off, afternoon pick-up, evening programming, and the spontaneous exchanges that carry the most weight
Develop a community that both domestic and international families regard as worth protecting—where advocacy arises organically from the quality of the experience
Communicate Alpha's narrative persuasively—in individual discussions, at gatherings, and within the circles of discerning, globally oriented families where the school's standing is truly established

What You Won’t Be Doing

Operating from behind a desk—your physical presence within the community defines the role
Adhering to standard 9–5 schedules—early starts, late afternoons, and evening commitments are integral to the position, not occasional requirements
Escalating challenging parent discussions to faculty or administrative staff—you retain full ownership of these interactions
Relying on administrative infrastructure, established procedures, or a complete team—you'll function with substantial autonomy and create systems as needed
Approaching family relationships as transactional accounts—this role values authentic connection over procedural adherence

Director Of Development Key Responsibilities

Serve as the central trusted relationship for every family's experience at Alpha's Miami campus and as the architect of the surrounding community culture. Maintain their confidence during difficult moments, establish the traditions and tone that make belonging feel meaningful, and foster the environment where satisfied families naturally become active advocates within the networks that influence Miami's private education landscape.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building and maintaining trust with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families in a relationship-intensive, high-touch capacity
Demonstrated success guiding sophisticated clients through consequential decisions—with measurable outcomes you can reference: conversion rates, retention figures, referral generation
The discretion and poise to navigate sensitive, confidential matters without causing lasting friction
Proven experience managing and developing personnel—providing coaching, maintaining rigorous standards, and executing difficult staffing decisions—beyond simply managing relationships or client portfolios
Innate cross-cultural competence working with both globally mobile and established Miami-based families
AI-native approach—you operate AI tools with fluency, understand their strengths and limitations, and actively identify superior alternatives, even without building them yourself
Located in Miami, available for full-time on-site engagement, and willing to work variable hours
Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Background as a head of school, principal, superintendent, or in equivalent educational leadership capacity
Professional-level fluency in Spanish or Portuguese
Personal or professional exposure to independent or non-traditional educational models
Established connections within Miami's private school parent communities
Experience working with internationally mobile, Latin American, or globally connected family populations
A personal network extending into the neighborhoods, clubs, and institutions where Alpha families reside and make decisions

jobs.title: Deputy Director of External Affairs
jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Deputy Director of External Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs is responsible for developing and executing the External Affairs department’s public affairs strategy. In this capacity, this individual provides advice, insight, analysis, coordination, and acts as a liaison between the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) and various government and regional stakeholders.

The Deputy Director is tasked with overseeing and managing the External Affairs department’s government affairs and external engagement strategies. As a leader on the External Affairs team, this person is responsible for serving as a liaison to many of the governmental agencies, partners, and service providers with which the Authority maintains relationships. Advises senior leadership on possible strategies for effectively managing governmental and interjurisdictional relationships for the benefit of the Authority's interests. Maintains constant vigilance on how the plans and activities of the Authority may interact with other stakeholder interests, and how external initiatives may impact the Authority. This position may also act as the department lead on various projects and programs that require coordination with cross-functional MBTA staff, consultants, and external organizations.

Duties & Responsibilities

Directs the operations of the Authority’s government affairs strategy by developing and advancing the MBTA’s legislative agenda in conjunction with other department leaders.
Works with department Leads and Senior Leadership in identifying and solving problems with governmental entities and/or introducing opportunities to promote the MBTA's reputation.
Represents the MBTA's interests with various government agencies, and state and local elected officials.
Acts as primary point of contact for state and local officials regarding issues related to any MBTA matter, including operations and capital projects.
Works with the Director of Capital and Community Relations to advise on and set strategic external engagement objectives related to capital projects.
Sets direction on capital project engagement related to government stakeholders.
Facilitates external communications, organizes meetings and materials, and maintains internal records.
Supports department management with drafting and submitting statutorily required legislative reports.
Assists colleagues on the External Affairs team with constituent requests.
Assists with the development and execution of outreach plans and external engagement strategies related to MBTA service, projects, and initiatives.
Monitors state legislation, analyzes legislative proposals, and provides updates and recommendations for the Assistant General Manager for External Affairs.
Maintain updated contact lists of regional stakeholders, elected officials, and staff.
Support the management and delivery of effective, timely completion of departmental and functional key initiatives, programs, and policies.
Works closely with the Office of Communications, Customer Experience, and other external-facing departments to ensure effective and proactive communication on a range of MBTA projects and events.
Attends external events as directed.
Handle all sensitive information in a strictly confidential manner.

Supervision

Will supervise Manager of Intergovernmental Affairs

*This job posting will close once it reaches 50
applications

or after
2 weeks

, whichever comes first.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution, in Political Science, Public Policy, Public Administration, Communications or related field.
Five (5) years of full-time experience working in a legislative office, government agency, and/or advocacy organization.
Two (2) years of leadership and/or supervisory experience.
Excellent written and oral communications skills, with ability to communicate effectively across departments and functions.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
Ability to support multiple assignments and stakeholders, prioritize workload for self, and coordinate with managers to meet deadlines.
Ability to organize data and excerise effective problem solving.
Ability to work effectively and collaboratively with a diverse workforce.
Have the maturity and confidence to interact with elected officials and staff.
Ability to travel to locations throughout the MBTA’s service areas.
Demonstrated interest in public transportation.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years prior to the closing date of this posting, including overall employment, job performance, discipline and safety records (infractions and/ or offenses occurring after the closing of this posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).

Substitutions

A High School Diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
An associate’s degree from an accredited institution and an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
A master’s degree in a related subject substitutes for two (2) years of general experience.
A nationally recognized certification, or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one year of experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

Master's degree from an accredited institution in Public Administration, Business Administration, Communications, or related degree.
Experience developing and delivering presentations to senior level executives.
Experience working in a large, matrixed organization.
Experience in local, state, or national politics/legislative affairs.

Job Conditions

Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.
Ability to work all shifts and / or locations assigned, directed, or necessary for this position, including (for some transit / operations roles) up to twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week as necessary to accommodate severe weather conditions, emergencies, or any other circumstances that may potentially impact service or the safety of service.
Intern / co-op staff must be enrolled full or part-time in an accredited educational program and maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 for the entire duration of the internship / co-op. Additionally, interns / co-ops must have valid work authorization and U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting pre-employment screenings / pre-boarding, working in their positions, and throughout the duration of their program.

Disclaimers And Definitions

General Disclaimer: The statements contained in this job description are intended to describe a summary, general nature, and complexity of typical job functions and do not represent an exhaustive list of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities required of staff assigned to this position.
Application Completion: It is each applicant’s responsibility to ensure application details are entered completely and correctly, including updated work and education histories (past and current). Incomplete applications may not be considered. Attachments do not substitute for application fields. The recruitment team does not have access to existing employee data / history.
Application Deadlines: Applicants should apply as soon as possible, as the MBTA may stop considering applicants after a sufficiently large applicant pool is established.
Work Environment: The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here-in are representative of those an employee may encounter while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. See job description for role-specific requirements.
Work Eligibility: All employees must be legally authorized to work in the United States and on an unrestricted basis. The MBTA does not have an employer work sponsorship program. However, if you have unrestricted work authorization, or are sponsored by a separate entity, you are welcome to apply. Further, all persons hired will require a U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting the position and employees will be required to complete a Form I-9 to verify their identity and eligibility to work in the U.S.

Candidates who do not attend their interview without advance authorization, including an email confirmation of a rescheduled time/date from Human Resources, will be considered a no-show and disqualified from consideration for the position. Related to rescheduling, on a one-time basis, and due to something emergent, you may be allowed to reschedule the interview. In addition, Human Resources may require documentation supporting the request. However, should you need to reschedule, you will need to contact your Recruiter directly by email.
Safety Sensitive Positions: Employees working in this classification will be subject to periodic physical examinations plus random drug and alcohol testing.

We have an exciting and rewarding opportunity for a RN Hospice Executive Director to join our leadership team. This role is ideal for a licensed Registered Nurse (RN) with strong leadership experience in hospice care, home health, or clinical operations management.

jobs.title: Director of Partnerships and Community Outreach, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
On-site (multiple locations listed in Requirements)
W2 Employee
$200K annually

The families who select Alpha rely on trusted advisors across every facet of their lives. This is the one role that has been absent.

You will be the person they reach out to when uncertainty arises, when intuition tells them something is amiss, or when they wish to share a moment they know you will appreciate. You will understand each family deeply enough to recognize their needs before articulation—and you will possess the judgment and composure to address what they present with care, discretion, and apparent ease. Over time, you will transcend being merely part of their child's school. You will become woven into the way they experience this phase of their family's journey.

Trust of this caliber does not emerge from procedure. It develops through presence—daily, steady, unhurried. You will be visible during morning arrival and afternoon departure, at evening gatherings that hold significance, and in the private conversations that rarely appear on any schedule. You will cultivate a community that families wish to safeguard, where membership feels natural and referrals occur because the quality of the experience compels them.

Alpha operates outside traditional school paradigms. Students complete core academic work in two hours daily through AI-driven applications, then dedicate remaining time to public speaking, critical thinking, and practical projects. No lectures. No filler assignments. Top 1% outcomes nationally. The families who enroll are investing in something they value deeply—but conviction requires cultivation.

You will maintain that dialogue with each family, through every uncertainty, for the duration of their child's enrollment. If advocating for an unconventional model to discerning skeptics feels like an obstacle, this position is not suitable. If it feels like the most compelling dialogue you could engage in, continue reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Take full ownership of the relationship with every family at your campus—the evolving, deepening bond that ensures parents feel recognized, not merely attended to
Identify concerns before they surface as issues, and address them with the discretion and interpersonal skill that preserves trust
Maintain visible presence in family spaces: morning arrival (7–9am), afternoon departure (2–4pm), evening parent gatherings, and select weekend programming
Develop a campus community with authentic depth—programs, customs, and engagement points that foster a sense of belonging to something worth defending
Cultivate parent advocates naturally, designing experiences of such consistent quality that referrals emerge as an organic result
Sustain the ongoing dialogue about Alpha's AI-powered approach with families managing screen time questions, skeptical relatives, and periods of uncertainty—not only during enrollment, but across their entire campus experience
Recognize when a family does not align with the community and manage that situation with the same professionalism you apply throughout—preserving the community is integral to serving it
Establish the systems and routines this position demands in a setting where the blueprint is still being developed

What You Won’t Be Doing

Overseeing enrollment—that falls under the Admissions Director; your work commences when families enroll and evolves continuously thereafter
Operating from a desk—your physical presence within the community defines the role
Adhering to standard 9–5 schedules—early mornings, late afternoons, and evening programming are fundamental, not occasional
Relying on administrative infrastructure, established protocols, or a complete team—you function with significant autonomy and create what is necessary
Approaching family relationships as accounts requiring management—this position values authentic connection over procedural adherence

Director Of Partnerships And Community Outreach Key Responsibilities

Serve as the trusted relationship anchor for every family's Alpha experience. Maintain their confidence during challenging periods, develop a community where belonging feels meaningful, and establish conditions under which satisfied families naturally become enthusiastic advocates.

Basic Requirements

Currently live within commuting range of one of these locations OR willing to relocate within 60 days (preference given to candidates with established local community ties): Denver, CO; Greenwich, CT; Boca Raton, FL; Tampa, FL; Boston, MA; Bethesda, MD; Charlotte, NC; Las Vegas, NV; Oklahoma City, OK; Tulsa, OK; Nashville, TN; Austin, TX; Dallas (Carrollton), TX; Fort Worth, TX; Houston (The Woodlands), TX; Park City, UT; Burlington, VT; Kirkland, WA; or Jackson Hole, WY
Legally authorized for U.S. employment without sponsorship requirements
5+ years in a relationship-focused role working with high-net-worth or ultra-high-net-worth families—private school admissions, luxury hospitality, philanthropic work, or any context where discretion, warmth, and interpersonal fluency mattered as much as competence
Proven capacity to sustain relationships through challenging situations with sophisticated families while maintaining trust
Authentic presence and communication approach that builds confidence rapidly with affluent, high-expectation families—genuine rather than rehearsed
Direct familiarity with independent, private, or alternative education—either professionally or as a parent—that provides legitimate credibility when families challenge the model
Authentic conviction in AI-powered education and capacity to carry that belief genuinely across years of parent relationships, extending well beyond initial enrollment discussions
Flexibility for non-standard hours: early mornings (7–9am), late afternoons (2–4pm), evening events 2–3x monthly, and occasional weekend activities

Nice-to-have Requirements

California will define the next decade of climate action, and the resources behind that work have to keep pace. Four-day work week for most of the year with five-day weeks during peak periods

Lead and develop the institutional giving team

Support in the execution of an annual institutional giving strategy aligned with organizational priorities and revenue goals

Seven or more years of institutional fundraising experience in a nonprofit environment, including demonstrated success securing and renewing five- and six-figure grants
